body:
*Written by the Stylfixx team · Reviewed by Omar Sharieff, Director, Stylfixx Innovations Pvt. Ltd. · Last updated 13 November 2026*

**Quick answer:** to hire a renovation contractor in Bangalore, fix your scope first, get itemised quotes from three contractors for the same scope, check each one's GST registration, a finished project and two past clients, and sign a written contract with stage-linked payments and a small advance. The biggest red flags are a quote far below the others, vague specifications such as "standard brand", and a request for a large advance before any work starts.

This guide walks through the process step by step, with a checklist you can use when you meet contractors, the red flags to watch for, and how to decide between one contractor for everything and separate trades.

## Step 1: Fix your scope before you call anyone

Contractors can only quote like for like if they are pricing the same job. Before the first site visit, write down:

- **The rooms and work:** for example, two bathrooms, kitchen, flooring in the living room, rewiring.
- **What must stay:** wardrobes, a floor you like, fittings you have already bought.
- **Your budget range:** a rough figure helps contractors suggest the right materials. For context, renovation in Bangalore typically costs ₹300–₹600 per sq ft for a refresh, ₹800–₹1,500 for a mid-level job and ₹1,500–₹2,500+ for a full renovation. Our [home renovation page](/service/home-renovations) explains each level.
- **Your dates:** when you can move out, if you need to, and any deadline such as a family event.
- **Building rules:** for flats, your society's working hours and approval process. See [apartment renovation](/service/apartment-renovation) for what associations usually ask for.

If you are not sure whether to renovate at all, read [renovate or rebuild an old house](/blog/renovate-or-rebuild-old-house) first.

## Step 2: One contractor for everything, or separate trades?

| | One design-and-build contractor | Separate contractors for each trade |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who is responsible | One company for design, civil, plumbing, electrical and finishes | You, or an architect, coordinating each trade |
| Your time | Low: one supervisor and one schedule | High: you schedule trades and settle disputes between them |
| Price visibility | Good if the quote is itemised; poor if it is one package price | Good: each trade quotes its own items |
| Delays | Fewer gaps between trades | Gaps when one trade waits for another |
| When something fails | One party to fix it | Trades can blame each other, for example plumber versus tiler over a leak |
| Best for | Most homeowners, especially for bathrooms, kitchens and full-flat jobs | Owners with time and site experience, or an architect supervising |

Separate contractors can cost less on paper, but the saving often disappears in rework, idle days and disputes. Whichever model you choose, insist on an itemised quote.

## Step 3: Shortlist three contractors and check them

| Check | How to do it | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GST registration | Ask for the GSTIN and check it on the GST portal | You get proper invoices, and the business is traceable |
| A finished project | Visit one completed job, ideally one that is a year or more old | You see how the work has held up, including waterproofing |
| Past clients | Call two clients yourself | Ask about delays, extra charges and how problems were handled |
| Who supervises | Ask who will be on site daily and who you call | Most problems come from unsupervised crews |
| Apartment experience | Ask how they handle society rules, lifts and debris | Avoids friction with your association |
| Office and contact details | A fixed office address and landline or verified number | You need to be able to reach them after handover |

## Step 4: Compare itemised quotes, line by line

A good renovation quote lists:

- **Every item with quantity, rate and amount**, room by room.
- **Brands and grades**: tiles, sanitaryware, pipes (CPVC), wiring, plywood and paint, named rather than "standard" or "as per market".
- **Demolition and debris removal**, including carrying charges in apartments.
- **Waterproofing** method and a flood test of at least 24–48 hours for bathrooms and balconies.
- **Exclusions**: what is not included, such as loose furniture, appliances or electrical points beyond a fixed number.
- **GST**: whether the price includes it.
- **Timeline** with start and end dates for each stage.
- **Payment stages** and the **warranty** in writing.

When quotes differ a lot, put them side by side. The gap is usually explained by one missing line, most often waterproofing, plumbing replacement or debris removal.

## Step 5: Sign a written contract with stage payments

Pay against finished, inspected stages, not dates. A typical renovation schedule looks like this; the exact split is agreed in your contract:

| Stage | Typical share |
| --- | --- |
| Booking and mobilisation | About 10% |
| Demolition, plumbing and electrical work done | 20–25% |
| Waterproofing tested, flooring and wall tiling done | 20–25% |
| Carpentry, ceiling and painting done | 20–25% |
| Handover after the snag list is closed | 10–15% |

Also put in writing: the scope and quote as an annexure, how changes are priced and approved (in writing, before the work), who pays for damage to common areas, the warranty period, and how delays are handled.

## Red flags when hiring a renovation contractor

**Before you sign:**

- A quote far below the others, with no clear reason.
- Specifications such as "standard brand" or "good quality" instead of named brands.
- A request for a large advance, or the full material cost upfront.
- No written quote or contract, or "we'll sort it out as we go".
- No GST registration, or a request to pay cash without a bill.
- Pressure to decide today because of a "special rate".
- No finished project you can visit, and no past client you can call.

**While work is on site:**

- Requests for payment ahead of finished stages.
- Pipes, waterproofing or wiring closed up before you or a supervisor have seen them.
- New charges that were not agreed in writing.
- Different crews every day, or no supervisor on site.
- Materials delivered that don't match the brands in the quote.

## Bangalore-specific points

- **Apartments:** most societies need written notice, contractor details and agreed working hours before work starts, and some take a refundable deposit.
- **Structural changes:** removing or altering structural walls, columns or slabs needs a structural engineer and approval from the city corporation; internal finishing work usually does not.
- **Monsoon:** plan terrace and exterior work outside June to September, and allow extra drying time for plaster and paint.
- **Material lead times:** imported tiles, modular kitchens and uPVC windows can take a few weeks, so order them early.

## Your contractor checklist

Before you sign, make sure you have:

- The same written scope given to three contractors
- Three itemised quotes with brands, exclusions and GST stated
- GSTIN checked, one finished project visited, two past clients called
- A named site supervisor and contact number
- A written contract with stage payments, change rules, timeline and warranty
- Society approval, or structural approval if needed

title: How to Hire a Renovation Contractor in Bangalore: Checklist and Red Flags
description: Step-by-step guide to hiring a renovation contractor in Bangalore: checks, itemised quotes, payment stages, red flags, one contractor vs separate trades.

faqs.question: How much advance should I pay a renovation contractor?
faqs.answer: Keep the advance small, typically around 10% of the contract value for mobilisation, and pay the rest against finished, inspected stages. A request for a large advance or the full material cost upfront is a red flag.

faqs.question: How many quotes should I get for a renovation?
faqs.answer: Get at least three itemised quotes for the same written scope, so you can compare them line by line. Quotes for different scopes cannot be compared fairly.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to hire separate contractors for each trade?
faqs.answer: The individual quotes can look cheaper, but you take on the coordination, and delays, rework and disputes between trades often cancel the saving. One contractor for everything usually suits homeowners who do not have time to manage the site.

faqs.question: Should a renovation contractor have GST registration?
faqs.answer: Yes, for any sizeable job. Ask for the GSTIN, check it on the GST portal and insist on a proper tax invoice. It makes the business traceable and gives you a paper trail if something goes wrong.

faqs.question: What warranty should a renovation contractor give?
faqs.answer: Ask for the warranty period for workmanship and waterproofing in writing in the contract, separate from manufacturer warranties on tiles, sanitaryware and fittings, which should be passed on to you.

faqs.question: How do I start a home renovation?
faqs.answer: Write down the scope room by room, set a budget range and your dates, check your society or structural approval needs, then invite three contractors to quote on the same scope.
